paper.title: A Subexponential Time Algorithm for Elliptic Curve Discrete Logarithm

main_finding: A conditional ECDLP application of the same unverified D1 blackbox. It independently uses essentially the already-existing linear-edge macro-FFT frontend; it does not close or lower our actual contraction backend.

frontend_comparison.paper: Fermat ring Z/(2^J+1), canonical J+1-bit words; one balanced split of each DFT; point products; inverse transform; integer carries; O(d) edges and O(d^(3/4)) degree. Fused twiddle factors and hardcoded zero positions give <1100(d+1) edges, degree<136(d+1)^(3/4).
frontend_comparison.repository: MacroGraph has the same ordered producers/consumers, two forward/inverse transforms, separate explicit scale/twiddle vertices, point products, initial/terminal carry, exact canonical local predicates and equality subdivision. MacroGraphUnique and PublicFactorCount give unique extensions and ordinary ordered factor-pair bijection. MacroParameters.variableCount_le gives <=6400*ell and scopeBound_le_rpow gives <=512*ell^(3/4).
frontend_comparison.transfer: Same asymptotic mechanism, with different constants, index convention and physical graph ABI. Folding twiddles/omitting forced-zero wires could reduce constants but needs a new graph/predicate/port proof and does not remove the open D1 backend. Not a drop-in source identity.

exponent_comparison.paper: Expected time2^O(b/m + m*b/sqrt(log b)); m≈(log b)^(1/4) balances inverse terms and yields2^O(b/(log b)^(1/4)). The relation matrix and factor-base enumeration cost2^O(b/m), not polynomial in b.
exponent_comparison.goal: Deterministic all-semiprime total binary-input time2^(C*ell/sqrt(log(ell+2)))*(ell+1)^d, fixedC,d before all inputs. Direct single multiplication relation already has O(ell) edges, so conditionally D1 gives logarithmic saving1/2 without the ECDLP relation-collection loss.
exponent_comparison.conclusion: For equal input-bit scales, saving1/4 is weaker than saving1/2. Neither is a b^(1/4) or b^(1/2) exponent; these are powers of log b in the denominator. Problems differ, so this compares parameter mechanisms rather than proving a complexity reduction between ECDLP and factoring.

randomness_and_scope.paper: Las Vegas: random independent affine-hash seeds, random u/v target pairs, expected prime/square-root acquisition, and unbounded restarts. Deterministic decomposition solver and deterministic row dependency keep V uniform conditional on targets. Always-correct output does not imply deterministic worst-case time. Overall matrix space is subexponential, not polynomial, despite each D1 call using polynomial space.
randomness_and_scope.non_transfer: No same-rate deterministic seed search or worst-case total bound is supplied. Prime field, known prime group order and group relation extraction assumptions are not a semiprime-factor oracle. Fixing per-input good seeds would be advice, not the sought uniform finite program.

No demonstrated shortcut for our already physically acquired compact alphabet/occurrence/selected-key sources or remaining coefficient/counter stages.

Uniform actual entry evaluation on every Boolean port assignment takes (s+L)^b*2^(A*s^.9) time and (s+L)^b space.
openai_D1_verified_primary_statement.conclusion: Deterministic exact modular contraction in (s+L)^O(1)*2^O(s/sqrt(log s)) bit operations and polynomial(s+L) space. Constants depend only on fixed hypotheses.
openai_D1_verified_primary_statement.exact_count_specialization: For Boolean predicates set l=1 and P0>|E|, bounded by Cs after fixed scaling; count<=2^|E| then no modular wraparound. Polynomial-size descriptions and polynomial entry predicates satisfy the stated evaluator budget. Edge subdivision creates the required bipartition at constant-factor cost.
